newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS: Down on overnight futures fall.
newsitem.headline: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS: Down on overnight futures fall.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps were weaker around midday on Tuesday, on lower overnight futures prices and a perception Indonesia has completed its prompt diesel purchases, traders said.
November gas oil traded early Tuesday at $29.70, down from Monday's late quotes of $29.95/30.05. December traded at $29.25, down 30 cents from Monday's late levels.
Traders said the weaker gas oil tone was due to market belief that Indonesia has completed its November physical diesel purchases which amounted to six million barrels.
The early morning decline found some support from expectations that China would renew its buying.
November gas oil swaps were last quoted at $29.80/$29.85 and December at $29.25/$29.30, brokers said.
The fall in gas oil swaps was also attributed to weaker heating oil futures prices on NYMEX.
December heating oil fell 0.65 cent to 65.95 cents per gallon in New York and continued to be traded down on the after-hours ACCESS trading system to 65.70 at 0333 GMT.
December NYMEX crude futures closed down 24 cents at 22.79 in New York.

Fuel oil swaps were lower at midday, with November quoted at $115.75/$116.25 per tonne, from a day-earlier $116.00/$116.50 and December was at $115.25/$115.75, down from $116.00/$116.50, brokers said.
Naphtha was quoted at $21.60/21.75, down from Monday's close of $21.90/$22.10.
